questions.prompt: A student puts the player square and falling circle in ONE sprite. Explain why two separate sprites would make coding easier and identify one test proving the objects are controlled separately.
questions.rubricText: Holistic 0–100: 90–100 accurate, specific and independently justified with a feasible test; 70–89 Explains independent sprite code and describes a real test of separate behavior; 50–69 partially correct, missing important detail or validation; below 50 insufficient/contradictory evidence. Missing/unsubmitted is a separate nonnumeric state under RTS-02.
questions.rubricReason: The exact frozen prompt asks why separate sprites simplify coding and for a test of separate control. Its pinned Meets criterion requires independent sprite code plus a real separate-behavior test; the upper band adds specificity and justification, not an unseen project requirement.
questions.projectIndependentReason: The one-sprite scenario, definition of independently controlled sprite, and teacher selection/code-workspace demonstration supply the information needed. A student may propose dragging/selecting one sprite and observing the other without completing the Perform or coding next-day motion.
